_doc: Offline reading fixtures — the historical readings, classified, so that any
new reading gate / scaffold change can be validated WITHOUT spending a run.
Why this file exists: reading_regression.py compares SCORES of a completed
run against recorded baselines. A score only exists after an LLM run has been
paid for. So the question 'does this new gate/rule hurt reading?' could only
be answered with money. These fixtures answer it offline.
Acceptance rule for any new reading gate (see reading_process_metrics.py):
a 'good' fixture may only raise flag codes listed in its known_defects,
and at least one 'bad' fixture must go red.
A gate that greens everything has no discriminating power. A gate that reds a
good fixture for something NOT in its known_defects is a regression against a
reading already known to be correct.
known_defects exists because 'good' turned out to be too coarse a label. The
07-08 reading is 9/9 walls but 6/7 windows, and the chain-placement gate reds
it for exactly the defect that cost it that window. The gate is right; the
binary label was wrong. Recording the defect keeps the fixture useful as a
green baseline for every OTHER gate while staying honest about this one.
Paths point at in-repo run directories rather than copies. A moved or deleted
run makes --fixtures exit 2 by name instead of silently measuring fewer.

fixtures.label: good
fixtures.why: The ORIGIN of the CV toolbox: Sonnet built its own classical-CV pipeline on the spot (112 tool calls, 60 of them Bash — PIL crop, grey mask + row/column projection for wall lines, overall-dimension px/m calibration, scipy connected components for windows). NOT no-tooling, and NOT eyeballed. Kept as a green fixture but explicitly NOT a form baseline: self-made tooling is the SOURCE of the form, not an instance of it.

fixtures.label: good
fixtures.why: Weak model + CV toolbox + pilot review gate. The richest process trace in the repo: 92 CV sidecars, per-image calibration, 9 overlay_logger disposition ledgers.

fixtures.label: good

score.note: no gt existed at the time; user-verified by eye as the cleanest output the project has produced

fixtures.why: Same form as sm21_2026-07-07_haiku on a DIFFERENT building. Carries the most complete reading_summary.md in the repo (per-image calibration RMSE, honest-provenance ledger, repeatedly-null ledger, schema feedback).

fixtures.label: good
fixtures.why: Third model family reaching the same result with the same form — the evidence that the toolbox removed model strength as a variable.
fixtures.known_defects_note: Pure chain-arithmetic route with no pixel corroboration (0 of 70 strokes carry both). It transcribed sm21's top chain identically to 07-07 (segments 14.76, overall 15.00) but butted the segments end to end instead of placing the 0.24 m residual at the two unlabelled 120 mm partition bands, so the chain closes on 14.76 and every window after the first gap drifts -0.12 then -0.24 m. That is the 7th window it missed. Also 2f C_top (0.12 m) and 2f C_east (1.06 m).

fixtures.label: good
fixtures.why: The same form reproduced on the CURRENT tree. Known caveat: walls sit on measured centrelines (0.11-0.12 m inset) while windows sit at nominal positions — registered as R-2, invisible to the scorer.
fixtures.known_defects_note: R-2: walls sit on measured centrelines (0.11-0.12 m inset) while windows sit at nominal chain positions — two different bases in one artifact, which is why chain_explained_pct is 40% here against 97-100% for the other good fixtures. No flag catches it yet; a chain-vs-pixel reconciliation gate would. The scorer never compares the outer boundary, so it cost nothing.

fixtures.label: bad
fixtures.why: Weak model WITHOUT the toolbox. The control arm that shows the toolbox, not the model, is what moved.

fixtures.label: bad
fixtures.why: Eyeballed geometry: interior walls at 5.4/9.0/13.6 where the chain says 5.0/10.0, and 25 plan openings (gt has 15) including six under 0.6 m wide.

fixtures.label: bad
fixtures.why: Review-ring arm. Only 6 plan openings emitted where gt has 15, and 29% of coordinates are not explainable from its own transcribed chains. Kept because NO hard flag currently fires on it — it is the fixture that shows the flag set is incomplete.

fixtures.label: bad
fixtures.why: 22 walls drawn on 1f (gt has 10) off 14 transcribed dimensions — the over-draw failure mode, while every coordinate still lands on a transcribed endpoint. Kept precisely because chain-explainability alone does NOT catch it.

fixtures.label: bad
fixtures.why: Capability-uncapped arm: 135 dimensions transcribed but only 60% of coordinates are chain-explainable — transcribed and then ignored.

fixtures.label: bad

score.note: unscored; pilot approved while still wrong, review then lifted

fixtures.why: ZERO windows on both plan views, and 21 of 21 CV calls spent on one image while five images got none. F-64's canonical shape: a blank answer passes more gates than a wrong one.

fixtures.label: bad
fixtures.why: 28 dimensions transcribed across six images (good runs transcribe 142-166) — the drawing's own numbers were largely never read.

fixtures.label: bad
fixtures.why: Partial failure, same model family that scored 9/9 on 07-08. Failure mechanism observed live: split a two-axis calibration into two single-axis calls to silence the cross-axis warning (F-63).

fixtures.label: bad
fixtures.why: F-69: on the east wall the reader reported the solid PIERS between windows instead of the windows (every one matches a gt pier to within 0.15 m at both ends). Same artifact used the correct polarity on the north wall. First fixture for the polarity detector.
